title: Setting Up a Computer
subject: Computer Science
description: In this activity, you will look inside a computer, fit its main parts, and connect its devices to the right ports. Tip: Walk around the computer to see its back, where the cables connect.

observe.description: Observe the parts of a computer system, what each one does, and how they connect.

captions.text: A computer system is made of parts that work together. Some parts take data in, some process it, and some give information out.
The monitor is an output device. It shows us text, pictures, and video.
The keyboard and the mouse are input devices. We use them to type, to point, and to click.
The system unit holds the parts that process and store data. Let's lift off its cover and look inside.
The large circuit board is the motherboard. Every part connects to it, so the parts can share power and data.
This is the central processing unit, or CPU. It carries out instructions and does calculations. It is the brain of the computer.
These are the memory modules, called RAM. RAM holds the programs and data you are using right now. When the power goes off, RAM is emptied.
The storage drive keeps your files and programs, even when the computer is switched off.
The power supply unit changes electricity from the wall socket into the power that the parts need.
Now let's turn the system unit around. At the back are the ports, where the cables connect.
Each kind of cable has its own shape of port. A plug only fits the port that matches it, and only one way round.
The monitor cable goes into the HDMI port. The keyboard and mouse go into USB ports. The network cable goes into the LAN port.
Connect every cable first, and switch on the power last. Before you open a computer, always switch it off and unplug it.

explore.description: Fit the parts inside the system unit, then connect each device to its port. Hold a part to hear how to handle it.

exploreSteps.title: Build
exploreSteps.description: Fit the CPU, the RAM, and the storage drive into the motherboard. Touch and hold a part to hear how to handle it.

exploreSteps.title: Connect
exploreSteps.description: Walk to the back of the system unit. Drag each plug to the port that matches it. A plug only fits its own port.

parts.name: CPU
parts.text: the processor. Hold it by its edges. Line up the gold triangle with the triangle on the socket, then lower it in gently. Never press on the pins.

parts.name: RAM
parts.text: the computer's working memory. Hold it by its edges. Line up the notch with the key in the slot, then press down firmly until both clips click.

parts.name: Storage drive
parts.text: an M.2 solid state drive. Slide it into the M.2 slot at a small angle, then press it down and fix it with its screw.

parts.name: HDMI cable
parts.text: it carries picture and sound from the computer to the monitor. It has a flat plug with two slanted corners, so it fits only one way.

parts.name: Keyboard USB plug
parts.text: the keyboard's cable ends in a flat, rectangular USB plug. Push it into any USB port, with the plastic tongue facing the right way.

parts.name: Mouse USB plug
parts.text: the mouse also uses a USB plug. It goes into another USB port, next to the keyboard.

parts.name: Network cable
parts.text: an Ethernet cable connects the computer to the school network. Its plug clicks into the LAN port. Press the clip to take it out.

parts.name: Power cable
parts.text: it brings electricity from the wall socket to the power supply unit. Connect it last, after every other cable.
